maia: hey — after this morning's corp CA rotation the rust SDK client we ship is failing in our integration tests with `certificate verify failed: unknown certificate` :grimace:
maia: stack trace (truncated):
```
Error: TLS error: certificate verification failed (UnknownIssuer)
 at reqwest::async_impl::response::Response::error_for_status
```
maia: only started after the corp proxy started injecting a new MITM cert. anyone seen this in Rust specifically? :eyes:

devops-bot: automated notice: corporate CA rotation completed at 2026-03-10T09:10Z. If your services use pinned certs or embedded bundles, rotate them accordingly.

sahil: short-term: try pointing the process at the updated CA bundle — RUST/reqwest respects the `SSL_CERT_FILE` env var if using native TLS backend. e.g. `export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca-bundle.pem` then run tests. also `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` for some tools.

olivia: question: are you using rustls or native-tls under reqwest? rustls uses its own root store and won't read system certs by default. if you're on rustls you need to explicitly add the corp CA to the rustls RootCertStore.

jeff: corp proxy is doing TLS termination + MITM (sad). for mTLS flows this will definitely break client cert handshakes unless the proxy is configured for pass-through. if you need client auth, talk to infra — otherwise you have to trust the proxy ca in the client.

sahil: example for native-tls + reqwest (load cert from file):
```
let mut buf = std::fs::read("/etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca-bundle.pem").unwrap();
let cert = native_tls::Certificate::from_pem(&buf).unwrap();
let tls = native_tls::TlsConnector::builder().add_root_certificate(cert).build().unwrap();
let client = reqwest::Client::builder().use_native_tls().build().unwrap();
// make sure the runtime process sees SSL_CERT_FILE too
```
sahil: for rustls (tokio-rustls) you'd use `rustls::RootCertStore` and `webpki_roots` and add parse_pem file.

maia: tried SSL_CERT_FILE -> still failing, seems our release binary uses rustls behind the scenes (via `reqwest` feature). switching to native-tls locally fixed it.

olivia: two options: 1) vendor the corp CA into your release binary at build-time (embed PEM and add to rustls RootCertStore on startup) or 2) switch the client to native-tls so it inherits system store (may be easier short-term).

jeff: for long-term, if this is a customer-facing service we shouldn't rely on corp MITM workarounds. infra can put the build/test runners on a network path without the intercepting proxy for CI. filed internal ticket ENGOPS-4123 to allow proxy-bypass for CI agents.

maia: thanks all — will try switching the crate feature to native-tls in CI first, then if that lands we'll open a small PR to embed CA into rustls for the dedicated runtime. pinging @sahil for a quick review once I have the PR. :thumbsup:
maia: last bit — any quick debug commands you recommend? I used `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect mysvc:443 -servername mysvc` and saw the proxy cert chain which helped confirm MITM.

sahil: yep `openssl s_client` is great. also `curl -v --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca-bundle.pem https://mysvc` to confirm. and `openssl x509 -in /path/to/cert -noout -text` to inspect.

maia: perfect, thanks — I'll update here once CI green.
